who_can_apply: Teens. The program page does not state an age or grade rule.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the program page. The library's main phone number is 503-644-2197.
notes: The council meets on the first and third Thursdays, 5 to 6 PM, at Beaverton City Library Main. Members must attend meetings and events.
duration: Meets twice a month
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer credit. The number of hours is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Youth age 13 and older. You must agree to give at least 80 hours of service within one year of starting. You must attend an initial training held online.
how_to_apply: Fill out the RISE Youth Leader application online. Then attend the virtual training. Questions? Call Melissa Marcum-Fredrick at 503-619-3941.
notes: The same page lists a Junior Lifeguard program for ages 12 and up. It also lists community and cultural events for ages 14 and up.
duration: At least 80 hours within a year.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work. It can count for school community service hours.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 16 to 22 who have a disability. You must be able to do light physical work about 6 hours a day, with some accommodations.
how_to_apply: Send in the online application and wait for staff to confirm. You hear after the application closes. Then you get sign-up papers. You go to a virtual orientation, with a parent or guardian if you are under 18.
notes: Campers must be dropped off and picked up at the camp area. Up to 8 campers may do 2 extra weeks with COYCC crews.
duration: 1 week (Week 1: July 12 to 16, 2027. Week 2: July 19 to 23, 2027)
pay_detail: $16 per hour. T-shirt, work shirt, safety gear, tools, camping equipment and food are provided.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 16 to 22 with different abilities. You can have been to Camp LEAD or want to go.
how_to_apply: Submit the online application. Staff will confirm they got it. You may need photo ID and proof of citizenship papers for I-9 checks, and bank details for direct deposit. Call 541-633-7834 with questions.
notes: The page says applications reopen in the fall. Check back soon. The page states $16 an hour.
duration: 1 to 2 Saturdays a month for 4 months
pay_detail: Paid wages. The hourly amount is not stated on this page.

who_can_apply: Central Oregon youth ages 16 to 18. You need photo ID and papers that show you can legally work (for example a signed Social Security card or birth certificate) for I-9 checks. Staff can help if you are missing documents.
how_to_apply: Send in the online application. Go to a local info session in April or early May. If you are picked, you hear back by mid-May. Then you do a virtual orientation and fill out job papers, with direct deposit.
notes: Call 541-633-7834 with questions. The page lists the application deadline as June but the full date is not shown. Crews work at seven central Oregon locations.
duration: 8 weeks, Monday to Thursday, 7am to 4:30pm (2027: June 21 to August 12)
pay_detail: $16 per hour. You may also earn 0.5 to 1 high school credit depending on your school.

who_can_apply: Oregon middle and high school students ages 12 to 18. A parent or guardian fills out the interest form. Spots go by lottery and a student can attend only one camp per summer.
how_to_apply: A parent or guardian sends in the High School Registration Form for the camps the student wants. A lottery picks who gets in. The parent hears back.
notes: Lane also runs free summer academies for students of color in Lane County. They are called Rites of Passage. There are 4 of them. They are African American, Asian and Pacific Islander, Bridge of the Gods and Puertas Abiertas. See the Lane Community Education pages.
duration: Monday to Thursday, about 4 days (2026 high school dates: Aug 10 to 13 and Aug 24 to 27)
pay_detail: Free. Transportation and food are on your own; parking is free and LTD buses come to campus.

who_can_apply: Applicants ages 16 to 21 who can work in a group of young adults from different backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Fill out the interest form on the Lane-Metro Youth Corps page. You get more info and a form to apply.
notes: The program page has no date (it has a 2021 example). Confirm the current ages, pay and dates with Looking Glass before you apply. School credit is available. It runs with the Oregon Youth Conservation Corps. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: 9 weeks, 32 hours a week
pay_detail: Paid. Hourly rate not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 24 who are low-income and face barriers to employment.
how_to_apply: Complete the interest form on the Job Training Program page. Questions: Hailey Johnston, 458-319-2968, hailey.johnston@lookingglass.us.
notes: Office: Riverfront Career Center, 1666 West 12th Avenue, Eugene. Bus passes or gas cards are offered. Spanish speaking case managers are there. Funded by WIOA. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: Youth are usually in the program a year or two; must meet a case manager at least once a month
pay_detail: $17 per hour for the paid work experience, limited to one placement capped at 200 hours.

who_can_apply: Ages 16 to 18. No experience needed. Crews start and end in Eugene, OR or Boise, ID. You provide your own transportation to and from orientation.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the Youth Camping page (Northwest Youth Corps application site). Contact info@nwyouthcorps.org.
notes: This is hard: you camp and work in all weather. If you leave before graduation you get a share of the stipend and lose the bonuses. The page lists possible high school credit. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: 4 to 5 weeks living outdoors (2026: June 13 to July 18; July 25 to Aug 29 or 30)
pay_detail: Up to $450 a week with bonuses, after $70 a week is deducted for food. $300 tuition fee, with need-based assistance.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18 in the Eugene area. Teens commute to a central meeting place each day; local housing is not provided.
how_to_apply: Use the Eugene Apply link on the program page (Northwest Youth Corps application site). Contact info@nwyouthcorps.org.
notes: Possible high school credit (ask your counselor). Same program also runs in Boise and Tacoma. Dates may change. NYC is based in Eugene. Oregon BOLI says minors age 14 to 17 are not issued individual work permits in Oregon (employers need a certificate to employ minors). A sibling card for the Tacoma crew uses the youth-ucf page; this card uses the program guide so the urls differ.
duration: 5 weeks, Monday to Friday, about 32 work hours a week (2026 Oregon: June 15 to July 17 or July 21 to Aug 21)
pay_detail: Stipend of $96 a day (up to $480 a week) plus $20 dependability and $20 safety weekly bonuses. Tuition fee $200, with need-based assistance.

who_can_apply: The page says volunteers range from high school students to retirees. A minimum age is not stated; ask the Science Center. A criminal background check is part of onboarding.
how_to_apply: Use Apply Now on the volunteer page. Then go to a volunteer orientation.
notes: The page gives no minimum age. It lists high school students among volunteers. Email the Science Center to ask if your age is OK for the role you want. The volunteer page now sends you to eugenesciencecenter.org/volunteer.
duration: Scheduled shifts after an orientation; length not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. Perks include a free membership after 40 hours of service and free planetarium shows.

who_can_apply: Oregon residents in high school who have low income (for example SNAP, WIC, TANF or Pell eligible). Live on campus program: rising juniors and seniors. Day program: any rising 9th to 12th grader.
how_to_apply: Check that you qualify. Pick a program. Use the Register Here link on the SAIL page when sign up opens.
notes: You can get high school credit. Sign up early because programs fill.
duration: One week (2026: residential July 12 to 17; day program July 20 to 24)
pay_detail: Free summer program. UO scholarship opportunities are listed.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 5 to 19. On Oahu, fill out the Oahu County 4-H Interest Form to join a club or program.
how_to_apply: On Oahu, fill out the Oahu County 4-H Interest Form. On other islands, use the Contact page on the Hawaii 4-H site to find your county program. Email Christine at chanakaw@hawaii.edu with Oahu questions.
notes: About 4,000 youth take part each year across the state. Meetings can be in homes, schools or community buildings. Oahu also lists day camps, shooting sports and a garden center program.
duration: Ongoing
pay_detail: Not stated on the program pages.

who_can_apply: High school students in Hawaii public schools (HIDOE). The program page does not state grades or ages. It covers 13 career and technical education pathways statewide.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the program page. Call the HIDOE main line at 808-784-6200 or ask your school.
notes: Act 251 (2025) gave $1.8 million for fiscal years 2025-26 and 2026-27. The state pays companies back for the time they spend training and supervising interns. No program contact is listed besides the main HIDOE phone line.
duration: 4 to 6 weeks in summer 2026 (6 weeks at 24 hours a week at the Pearl Harbor Aviation Museum; 4 weeks at 32 hours a week at Aloun Farms)
pay_detail: $20 minimum hourly wage

who_can_apply: Students who are at least 16. Summer 2026 was for high school sophomores (Class of 2028), juniors (Class of 2027), or students in a Community School for Adults. A program of study that fits the internship is preferred.
how_to_apply: Download the Student Intern Casual Employment Application and fill it out. Email it to the contact for the internship you want, or drop off a paper copy. High school internships are only for students at that school.
notes: The positions list is a separate sheet linked from the program page.
duration: Dates and hours vary by internship. Summer 2026 ran June to July.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Most positions need participants to be 17 to 38 for the whole term. A small number of positions have no upper age limit.
how_to_apply: Apply online with the Apply link on the Kupu Aina Corps page. Look at the host sites you can pick.
notes: Most positions take ages 17 to 38 for the whole term. Jobs are on Hawaii Island, Kauai, Maui, Molokai and Oahu. The older HYCC Summer program (17 and up) is paused. Kupu also runs the Conservation Leadership Development Program. Hawaii requires a child labor certificate (work permit) for working minors under 18. It is free. It is a Certificate of Employment for 14 and 15, and a Certificate of Age for 16 and 17.
duration: 6 or 12 month terms, part-time (20 hours a week) or full-time (40 hours a week)
pay_detail: $20 an hour, plus health insurance for 20+ hours a week, a retention bonus ($200 to $800) and paid time off.

who_can_apply: Juniors and seniors in good academic standing. The program page gives no age rule.
how_to_apply: Send an application, a resume, a news-style writing sample and one recommendation letter. You can apply online through the link on the page, or mail or email the materials. Phone: 808-586-9490.
notes: This is one lawmaker's office. The page does not say if you must live in her district. The email link on the page may point to the wrong address, so use the phone number to confirm.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: The program page says these are non-paid positions.

who_can_apply: Hawaii students at public, private, charter or homeschool. You need a GPA of 2.5 or better and email access. Students in their last year of school get strong preference.
how_to_apply: Check the program page in spring 2027 for the new application. Questions: HighSchool_Internship@schatz.senate.gov or the Hawaii office at 808-523-2061.
notes: Interns are picked for work in the community and a mix of interests. You do not need student government experience. This program is virtual.
duration: Late September through April. You must commit to the full term.
pay_detail: Pay is not stated for the high school internship on the program page.

who_can_apply: Students at a participating Hawaii public high school. Each high school decides which classes it offers, so ask your counselor.
how_to_apply: Meet with your high school counselor first. Then fill out the UH System application and the online Dual Credit Application. Get the signatures, and send both to the UH campus by its deadline.
notes: The program page says 53 public high schools offered Early College in the 2023 to 2024 school year. Classes are face to face, online or mixed. Classes at the 100 level and above earn college credit.
duration: Classes run during the school year
pay_detail: Free to students at Hawaii public schools in the program, thanks to state funding. You are not paid.

who_can_apply: Students at a Hawaii public or charter high school who meet the college campus admission rules and are under 21 on September 1 of the school year. UH Manoa does not take part in Running Start.
how_to_apply: Meet with your high school counselor first. Then fill out the UH System application and the online Dual Credit Application. Get the signatures, and send both to the UH campus by its deadline.
notes: Nine UH campuses take part. You must also pass the placement tests the campus asks for. Private school students may be able to use an Early Admit program instead. Ask the UH campus.
duration: One college class per term in fall, spring or summer
pay_detail: Varies. Student or family, the high school, or a scholarship may pay. A GEAR UP scholarship for students with low family income covers tuition, fees and books for one class, but the page says it will not be offered after the Summer 2026 term.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 24. Many of the youth in the farm programs come from Latino and Latine backgrounds.
how_to_apply: Check the Hiring page in late January 2027 and sign up for the farm newsletter to hear about postings.
notes: The page does not give the season dates or pay. Confirm both when applications open.
duration: Seasonal
pay_detail: Youth earn income. The hourly rate is not stated on the program page.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be 16 or older. The online form also asks you to say you are over 18, so ask the group which rule applies to a 16 or 17 year old.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer form, or print the PDF form and mail it in. Then go to an orientation. Questions: admin@friendsofthelibraryofhawaii.org.
notes: This is the Friends group, not the state library system. The state library page says to contact your local branch to ask how you might participate.
duration: Not stated. Commitments can be once a day, once a week, or as often as you can come.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer work.

who_can_apply: Warehouse minimum age is 8. Anyone 15 or younger must come with an adult age 18 or older. Some distribution sites require 13 or 14 as the minimum age. Groups of three or more can apply.
how_to_apply: Sign up on the volunteer page for warehouse shifts. Or email volunteer@hawaiifoodbank.org to save a spot for a Saturday packing.
notes: The warehouse is at 2611 Kilihau St., Honolulu. All new warehouse volunteers must go to orientation. The page lists a minimum age of 13 or 14 for some sites where food is given out.
duration: Warehouse shifts Monday to Friday except holidays and the second Thursday afternoon of each month, plus Saturday packings. Shift length not stated.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer shifts.

who_can_apply: Volunteers must be at least 16. High school students (16 to 17) must commit to a regular weekly schedule for three months and complete onboarding health requirements.
how_to_apply: Download the High school form (Oahu and Kauai) from the Hawaii Pacific Health volunteer page. Email it to Volunteer Services. The page lists it in its volunteer section.
notes: Summer student applications close in early April and the page does not give a year. Other application windows are not stated on the page, so check back.
duration: 3 months for high school students, one weekly 4-hour shift (or two 2-hour shifts). Summer volunteers commit two months.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 15 to 17. Check each role in the Opportunities Directory for its age rule. Teens who cannot give a weekly shift for three months go through the Youth and Education Department instead.
how_to_apply: Pick a role in the Opportunities Directory. Finish the Junior Volunteer Application Process. It has a $15 Junior Volunteer Application Fee. Training has a 2 to 3 hour in person class and shadow shifts. You also take online courses that can take about 5 to 6 hours.
notes: The page does not state an application window or year. It says to check back and apply at a later time. Youth who want service hours can go through the Youth and Education Department.
duration: The page asks for a weekly shift for three months. Some roles need a teen to volunteer with an adult. Check each role for its time commitment.
pay_detail: Unpaid. There is a $15 Junior Volunteer Application Fee.

who_can_apply: Students. The page does not state ages or grades; check the application. Members serve a one-year term, volunteer at events and attend quarterly meetings.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teens4Animals Council form when it opens.
notes: Members attend quarterly meetings and field trips on topics such as responsible fishing and ethical farming. The page does not state an age or grade rule.
duration: One-year term (2026-2027), with 4-day summer training and quarterly meetings
pay_detail: Unpaid. The 4-day training fee is waived for council members.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 16 to 24 who lack support. The page lists who can get paid on the job training and help with job school costs. Check the Apply Here link for the full list of rules.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Here link on the Kupu Community Program page.
notes: It is based at the Hookupu Center in Kewalo Basin Harbor, Honolulu. It works with Honolulu District public schools and McKinley School for Adults. They help with the diploma and with HiSET or GED tests.
duration: Year-long program
pay_detail: Not stated as a wage. The page lists eligibility for paid on-the-job training placements and/or financial help with vocational training.

who_can_apply: Hawaii residents who are 16 by the start, have finished sophomore year, and are full-time high school students. Students from any island can apply but must pay for their own housing and travel.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application. Email it with your unofficial transcript, one letter of recommendation and an essay of 500 to 700 words. Send it to ltgov.internships@hawaii.gov. Some students are then interviewed.
notes: Very small group: the page says six students are picked. The page and form differ on the start date (June 15 or June 16), and its FAQ still shows some 2025 dates, so confirm with the office.
duration: 5 weeks, Tuesdays and Thursdays, 9am to noon
pay_detail: Unpaid. Parking is not provided.

who_can_apply: The application has a box for high school students and a parent or guardian consent part. The program page does not state a minimum age.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online volunteer application. High school students check the high school box. A parent or guardian signs the consent part. Expect a short interview and a background check.
notes: The museum matches volunteers to openings, so you may wait to hear back. Teen roles are not described on the main program page. The older application form is what shows the high school box, the parent consent part, the background check and the interview.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Students now in high school or the same level. Rising seniors get first pick. Your application is checked through the OHA Hawaiian Registry Program. A parent or guardian fills it out with you.
how_to_apply: Watch the program page for the online application. You write short answers and an essay, and a teacher, counselor, mentor or boss fills out a recommender form. New applicants also finish the Hawaiian Registry Program application. Call (808) 594-1835 for help.
notes: The program page does not spell out an ancestry rule, but it uses the Hawaiian Registry Program to verify applicants. Ask OHA if you are not sure you qualify. You get yourself to the airport.
duration: Six days, overnight. The 2026 program ran June 21 to 26.
pay_detail: Free for chosen students. OHA pays interisland airfare, lodging, meals and program travel. You are not paid.

who_can_apply: Junior Leaders must be 13 before August 1 and no older than 17 by the camp end date (2026: July 24).
how_to_apply: Contact your local Summer Fun site (see the Summer Fun site map). Sign up as a Junior Leader.
notes: The page does not say whether junior leaders are paid or whether their hours count as volunteer service. Ask the site.
duration: 2026 program ran June 8 to July 24
pay_detail: Pay not stated on the page. Paid summer aide jobs are listed separately (see the Summer Swim Aide card).

who_can_apply: Open to applicants as young as 16. You need a valid American Red Cross Lifeguard Training, First Aid and CPR/AED for the Professional Rescuer certificate. You also need work with children and teens.
how_to_apply: Apply through the online application link on the Summer Fun Jobs page.
notes: Work sites: 21 pools and 3 ocean recreation sites. Hawaii requires a child labor certificate (work permit) for working minors under 18. It is free. It is a Certificate of Employment for 14 and 15, and a Certificate of Age for 16 and 17.
duration: Seasonal full-time or part-time. The page does not give start or end dates.
pay_detail: $19.23 an hour

who_can_apply: Teens 15 to 17 need parent permission and a shot record for MMR and varicella. All volunteers commit to at least 100 hours.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteers form (or the High School Summer Student Program form) linked on the Queen's volunteer page. Or call Volunteer Services (Monday to Friday, 8 am to 4 pm).
notes: The page lists Teen Volunteer forms for 3 sites. They are Queen's Medical Center, Queen's West O'ahu and Queen's North Hawai'i Community Hospital. The page does not say if applications are open now.
duration: At least 100 hours; summer student program also offered
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Students in grades 10 to 12 with a 2.8 or higher GPA, at a Hawaii high school that offers a UH Manoa course. A 2.8 GPA is a minimum and does not guarantee a spot.
how_to_apply: Talk to your high school college counselor first. The program page sends you to its How to Apply page for the steps.
notes: Your high school must offer a UH Manoa course. The college work is hard, and past grades in college classes may be looked at. This program was called Manoa Academy before.
duration: One college course per term
pay_detail: The program page says there are no tuition or fee costs to students. You are not paid.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12 and recent graduates. 24 spots.
how_to_apply: Use the application form on the Outreach College program page. Contact summer.programs@hawaii.edu or 808-956-9246.
notes: The cost is lower for Hawaii residents. Programs on Coconut Island run if the weather allows.
duration: One week (2026: June 1 to 5), with a boat from Heeia Kea Boat Harbor to Coconut Island each day, weather permitting
pay_detail: $750 for Hawaii residents, $1,500 for non-residents (2026).

who_can_apply: Students in grades 10 to 12. The page lists the program as a week-long summer program for students interested in health professions.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the Outreach College program page when the next application opens. Contact Noelani Ching, nching@hawaii.edu, 808-692-0948.
notes: The two pages show different prices. Confirm the cost when applications open.
duration: One week (2026: July 6 to 10)
pay_detail: $575 on the program page (Kamaaina discount of $50). The high school summary page lists $525 for Hawaii residents and $575 for non-residents.

who_can_apply: Students who will have finished their sophomore or junior year. You need a 3.5 GPA, the maturity for college work and approval from a parent or guardian.
how_to_apply: Apply to the Summer Scholar Program. Once you are in, sign up for UH Manoa summer classes. Contact sscholar@hawaii.edu or 808-956-9246.
notes: No on-campus housing. Courses can be cancelled for low enrollment.
duration: Courses in sessions: May 26 to July 2, July 6 to Aug 14, or June 15 to July 24 (2026 dates)
pay_detail: Student pays tuition, fees and materials at UH Manoa resident undergraduate rates. A $1,200 need-based scholarship is available to Hawaii students who get free or reduced-price meals or school financial aid (first come, first served).

who_can_apply: High school students. The aquarium says regular volunteers must be 18, with exceptions for teen programs.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply link on the aquarium volunteer page when it is time. If you have a question, send an email to volunteer@waikikiaquarium.org.
notes: The page does not state the exact age range or application dates. The aquarium is open during repairs. Other aquarium volunteer roles are for 18 and older.
duration: One 4-hour shift a week for 5 weeks
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program.

who_can_apply: High school students in grades 9 to 12. The program page does not give other rules.
how_to_apply: Send your name through the interest form on the program page. If cost is a worry, use the Financial Assistance link on that page.
notes: Contact aball@ymcahonolulu.org. You can also use yaghawaii@ymcahonolulu.org. The page lists no cost or dates. Ask before you plan.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Cost is not stated on the program page. Need based scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Ages 14 to 24 at the time of appointment. If you are under 18, you need a parent or guardian's permission.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Honolulu Youth Commission application page. It reopens in 2027. If you are under 18, get a parent or guardian to say yes.
notes: Seats are chosen by the Mayor or by City Council members. An earlier call for applicants in July 2026 gave a July 22 deadline. Expect a similar time next year, but this is not confirmed.
duration: One or two year term, depending on who appoints you
pay_detail: Pay is not stated on the program page

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 16 who can volunteer at least one full week of Zoo Camp.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Application. Upload a signed Waiver of Liability and a current photo. Then set up an interview. It can be in person or on Zoom. Training is the general volunteer orientation and a zoo safety class.
notes: Regular zoo volunteer roles are 18 and older; this is the teen exception. Check the page for the current camp schedule.
duration: At least one full Zoo Camp week (Mon to Fri, 8:00 am to 2:30 pm, with extended hours to 5:30 pm). Camps run in spring, summer, fall and winter.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: High school students. Which option you can use depends on your high school. Talk to your high school counselor for course lists and deadlines.
how_to_apply: Early College Dual Credit: apply through your high school counselor. Early Admit: fill out the Early Admit forms. Then sign up for classes after you are accepted.
notes: The page says Early College has 2 options. Early College Dual Credit is usually classes at the high school. Early Admit is classes on the college campus. Compare the options on the page to pick one.
duration: By semester (fall, spring and summer)
pay_detail: Free or discounted tuition is available. Who pays varies: high school, student or family, or scholarship.

who_can_apply: You must be at least 14 by the program start date. You must be entering grades 9 to 12 (or home school at that level).
how_to_apply: Fill out the Volunteer Application. Go to an info session (online or in person). Chosen volunteers go to 3 days of training in person.
notes: The page does not state a set application window. Summer volunteers can also earn hours through trips and career activities. Contact: volunteer@aquarium.org.
duration: School-year program: 20 hours of training and 48 hours of volunteering in 4-hour shifts (68 total). Summer first-year program: 66 hours total.
pay_detail: Unpaid. No fees. Perks include a free aquarium membership after 50 hours and guest passes.

who_can_apply: Teens ages 14 to 19 who were in 4-H in the 2025-26 year (member, camp, event or in-school program) and have not attended a national 4-H event before. Must be able to travel to DC in March 2027 and to Portland airport. Oregon youth join a chaperoned group.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application form and upload a 2 to 4 minute video at beav.es/ignite2027 answering the prompt on the page. Do not use the national 4-h.org site.
notes: Requests for disability help are due Oct 31, 2026. This is a 4-H event named Ignite. It is not the same as the Ignition youth conference.
pay_detail: Event page lists $300. A donor covers a large part of the conference cost and airfare.

who_can_apply: County Ambassadors: contact your local 4-H office for rules. State Ambassadors: 4-H youth in the Senior age division who have been in 4-H at least one year. The page does not give the Senior division ages.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application (a fillable PDF) and upload it with the Qualtrics form. Ask your 4-H volunteer or office to review it first. Finalists interview at Summer Conference in Corvallis.
notes: The page says the 2026-2027 Ambassadors are announced on the last night of Summer Conference. The page does not give the Senior division ages. Ask your county 4-H office.
duration: One 4-H year
pay_detail: Unpaid leadership role

who_can_apply: Oregon 7th to 12th graders. You do not have to be a 4-H member.
how_to_apply: Register online when registration opens (about mid-May). Choose your workshops when you register. Watch for emails from your county 4-H program about financial help.
notes: 2026 dates were June 24 to 27 and registration opened May 15, 2026 at 3:00 pm. Buses leave from several Oregon towns for an added fee. 2027 dates not posted.
duration: 4 days (June 24 to 27 in 2026)
pay_detail: $275 registration fee plus a bus fee if you ride the bus. Financial assistance and transportation help are available through your local 4-H program.

who_can_apply: Oregon youth. Check with your local 4-H program coordinator to find a club and project that fit your area.
how_to_apply: Contact your local 4-H program coordinator. They will help you find a club. Then sign up online in 4-HOnline. Or return the paper forms to your county 4-H office.
notes: The page was written for the 2025-2026 4-H year. Not every project is offered in every county, since it depends on volunteers. To join in another county, you need an Out of County Participation Form.
duration: 4-H year starts October 1
pay_detail: Not stated on the page. Ask your county 4-H office about enrollment fees.

who_can_apply: Youth ages 14 to 17 who want a summer farm or ranch job. You must attend every session of your class.
how_to_apply: Pick a county class on the page and use its register link. Or contact Andrea Leao or your local Extension office.
notes: The page says Oregon requires farmers and ranchers who hire minors under 18 to be sure those minors passed tractor safety training. That is the page's own statement. Ask your boss. 2026 sites included Linn, Marion, Clackamas and Jefferson counties.
duration: 22 hours over 2 to 3 dates
pay_detail: $75 in most counties and $95 in Clackamas County (2026 prices).

who_can_apply: Age 16 or older. There is a scholarship for volunteers who meet its rules.
how_to_apply: Fill out the online form. Go to an orientation and interview. Finish the paperwork and a background check. Then do a health check with a TB test.
notes: The page gives a minimum age of 16 and no upper age limit. The page says to wait for the application to re-open for other Legacy medical centers. Usually the ask is one four-hour shift a week for one year.
duration: Usually one 4-hour shift a week for one year
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: High school students going into grades 9 to 12. Writing and Studio Art are for rising grades 10 to 12. The page lists grades, not ages.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Precollege Program Interest Form on the program page. For questions, email summercamps@lclark.edu.
notes: Summer 2027 costs are still being set. These programs do not give college credit. Students who finish a program and are later admitted get a guaranteed minimum of $20,000 a year in renewable scholarship funding.
duration: Varies by program. Writing and Studio Art run June 20 to July 3, 2027.
pay_detail: Costs listed for 2026: $1,800 for Circular Innovation, Data in Action and Future Health Leaders. $3,600 for Theatre. $3,800 for the Writing Workshop. $3,650 for Studio Art. A $500 deposit is not refundable. Some partial scholarships are available.

who_can_apply: Middle and high school students. (A separate Tween Council is for ages 9 to 12.) Minimum age beyond "middle school" is not stated.
how_to_apply: Not stated on the page. Ask staff at your neighborhood library, or contact Volunteer Services at 503-988-5731 or libvols@multcolib.org.
notes: Which branches have a council is not listed on the page, so confirm with your branch. The library's volunteer page lists Volunteer Services contact details.
duration: Meets twice a month; length of membership not stated
pay_detail: Unpaid. Members earn volunteer hours.

who_can_apply: Anyone age 10 and older can volunteer on their own. Younger volunteers must have a parent or caregiver with them.
how_to_apply: Apply online or on paper at any library. Share your name, contact details and area of interest. You do not need a Social Security number. The library contacts you to schedule an interview. Orientation and training come after you are accepted.
notes: This is the general library volunteer page. Current jobs are listed on an outside volunteer site. A link is on the page.
duration: Not stated on the program page
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Youth ages 13 to 21 who live, work, go to school or go to an after school program in Multnomah County or the City of Portland. Picks are based on drive and point of view, not grades or past leadership.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Apply to the Multnomah Youth Commission form on the county page. Ask for a reference. Meetings are 2 Sundays a month (4:30 to 7:30 pm) in Portland and Gresham. There is also a weekly after school meeting.
notes: The page was last reviewed February 2025, so confirm the current cycle. Reference letter due the same day as the application.
duration: Voting members give 12 hours a month; at-large members give 7 hours a month
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer (non-paid) positions.

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 18. You live in a northwest community where the program runs. The page names Portland area sites.
how_to_apply: Apply online through the Northwest Youth Corps site (Apply link on the program page). Ask info@nwyouthcorps.org about help with tuition and school credit.
notes: You may be able to earn high school credit. Your school decides, and requests are handled only after you finish. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: 5 weeks, Monday to Friday (2026: June 15 to July 17 or July 21 to Aug 21)
pay_detail: Stipend of $480 a week plus up to $40 a week in bonuses (up to $520). Tuition fee $200, with need-based assistance available.

who_can_apply: Oregon high school students entering grades 10, 11 or 12 who like health care careers.
how_to_apply: Use the apply link on the OHSU Experience page when it opens.
notes: Not a job and not paid. The page describes 2025 as a pilot year. The 2026 camp had three one-day sessions with the same activities each day.
duration: One day (2026 dates: Aug 18, 20 and 25, 9 am to 4 pm; each day is the same)
pay_detail: Free. Scholarships from the Oregon Health Authority cover the cost.

who_can_apply: High school or college students who are only free in summer. Guides and Healing Through Music volunteers must be 14 or older. Art Cart volunteers must be 16 or older and have experience with children.
how_to_apply: Apply when the 2027 Summer Program opens. The page says that is January 2027. Healing Through Music volunteers must audition. They must bring their own instrument, except piano.
notes: The page asks volunteers to pick up extra shifts beyond their weekly schedule. The page does not give summer 2026 shift dates or hours beyond the weekly minimum.
duration: At least 26 shifts, with 2 regular shifts a week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Oregon high school students. OHSU especially wants students from underserved and rural communities. Students at any Oregon high school may apply. Ages and grades are not stated. Students must meet health care worker shot rules.
how_to_apply: Send in a form. Also send a recommendation from a teacher, counselor, principal, adviser, coach or other teacher. If you have a question, you can send an email to knightscholars@ohsu.edu.
notes: Applications were closed when the page was read. Confirm whether a 2027 group is running before you plan around it. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: Introduction 1 week; Immersion 10 weeks; Intensive 10 weeks (each level requires finishing the one before)
pay_detail: Scholars are paid a stipend (amount not stated). OHSU also pays for hotel or residence hall housing during time in Portland.

who_can_apply: Counselors must be 16 or older by June 1. Limited housing is for counselors over 18 who live outside Portland.
how_to_apply: Use the Apply Now link on the OMSI Outdoors hiring page when the 2027 counselor job posts.
notes: Summer camp is overnight, and counselors stay with campers. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: Summer camp season; exact dates not stated
pay_detail: Paid. Counselor wage not stated (the page lists $135 to $180 a day only for full-season staff). Housing and meals are provided during programming.

who_can_apply: Teens 14 and older apply with the Teen Volunteer Application. Some roles list other age rules. For example, the planetarium usher must be 14 or older.
how_to_apply: Fill out the Teen Volunteer Application on the OMSI volunteer page. If you are over 18, you must also take a class for mandatory reporters.
notes: The page sorts roles into Ages 14+, 16+ and 18+ sections, so check each role's minimum age.
duration: Most roles need at least 4 hours a month for 3 months (some roles ask for more)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Any teen age 13 to 18. Museum admission is not required to use The Mezz.
how_to_apply: Just visit during open hours. Teens who want to help run it can apply as Mezz volunteers (see the OMSI teen volunteer card).
notes: The page says some exceptions apply to the listed hours. Ticketed programs are not offered. To visit the rest of the museum you need to pay admission.
duration: Open Tuesday to Sunday, 11 am to 5 pm, Sept 8, 2026 to June 13, 2027
pay_detail: Free for teens. Not a job.

who_can_apply: The volunteer FAQ sets a minimum age of 8. Each shift lists its own minimum age. First-time volunteers under 18 need a youth release form.
how_to_apply: Create a volunteer profile on the volunteer page. Then reserve a shift. Read the minimum age on each shift first.
notes: Check the minimum age on each shift. For small group or family volunteering, email volunteer@oregonfoodbank.org. Shoes must have closed toes and heels. Shirts must have sleeves.
duration: Single shifts, most days of the week
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role

who_can_apply: Youth ages 12 to 17 at the Portland campus. People who qualify go into a random lottery for limited spots.
how_to_apply: Send in the youth form during an application window. A lottery picks the spots.
notes: Confirm the window dates on the page, since the year is not printed. The page says applications for the Portland campus are closed now.
duration: One 2-hour shift every other week for at least 6 months (Wed to Sun 4 to 6 pm, plus weekend 10 am to noon)
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Teens from the Portland metro area who are 13 to 15 on April 12 of the program year. Selected by application and interview (about 30 teens).
how_to_apply: Apply online in January. Then interview. Chosen leaders go to an orientation and trainings in spring (the page lists March 29, April 12 and May 17).
notes: Ages 13 to 15 only. No direct animal contact in the first year. The page says the program does not guarantee future employment.
duration: 10 weeks; at least one 6-hour shift a week for 8 of the 10 weeks
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer program. No fees.

who_can_apply: Advancing high school juniors and seniors. The page does not state a minimum or maximum age.
how_to_apply: Sign up online. Use the Register link on the Pacific University Synapse page when it opens.
notes: Sessions are in Hillsboro (June 22 to 25) and Forest Grove (June 26) in 2026. The page does not list a cost.
duration: 2026: June 22 to 25, 9 am to 4 pm in Hillsboro; June 26, 9 am to 1 pm in Forest Grove
pay_detail: Cost not stated on the program page. Check the registration page.

who_can_apply: You must be 16 by the first day of class (no exceptions). Lifeguard candidates must pass a swim test. It has a 50 yard freestyle or breaststroke swim, a 50 yard rescue tube swim, a 10 pound brick pickup and 1 minute of treading water. Lifeguard and swim teacher classes are only for people who plan to apply to work for PP&R Aquatics.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a class on the aquatics page. Then apply for a pool job through the City of Portland job site (GovernmentJobs.com). You must be 16 to apply.
notes: Go to every session. If you miss a day you must take a new class. Your certificate must stay current while you work. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: Classes year-round; the city runs about 700 summer pool staff and up to 400 at indoor pools in other seasons
pay_detail: Paid city pool jobs. Hourly rate and class fee not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: The page says the bureau employs people aged 14 to 24. The minimum age depends on the job (pool jobs are 16 and older).
how_to_apply: Make an account on GovernmentJobs.com. Apply to the open Portland Parks & Recreation jobs.
notes: Check each job posting for its own minimum age. The page lists career fairs on March 24 and March 28, 2026. Oregon BOLI says minors age 14 to 17 are not issued individual work permits in Oregon (employers need a certificate to employ minors).
duration: Summer season; exact dates vary by job
pay_detail: Paid. Hourly rate not stated on this page.

who_can_apply: Young people ages 16 to 24. The page lists no other rules. Use the interest form to confirm you qualify.
how_to_apply: Complete the PDX Youth@Work Interest Form on the Worksystems page.
notes: It starts at age 16, so 14 and 15 year olds can not join. Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: Short-term SummerWorks jobs and year-round PDX Youth@Work experiences; length not stated
pay_detail: Paid. Hourly rate not stated on the page.

who_can_apply: Students ages 14 to 18 who have finished at least one year of high school.
how_to_apply: Apply online on a rolling basis until programs are full. Applications open fall 2026, per the page.
notes: The page does not list dollar amounts for tuition or scholarships.
duration: Intensives are 2 weeks and Studios are 1 week, 9 am to 4:30 pm Monday to Friday. 2027 sessions run July 12 to Aug 6.
pay_detail: Tuition (includes materials) for Summer 2027 will be announced when applications open this fall. Need-based scholarships and payment plans are available; early registration saves 10%.

who_can_apply: Crew members ages 14 to 18. The page does not list grade requirements. Crew leaders must be at least 18 and have a driver's license.
how_to_apply: Apply through the City of Portland job site when the crew member job posts.
notes: Crews: Trail (the hardest work on the body), Tree, Community Gardens, City Nature East, and West Side Nature (No Ivy League). Oregon BOLI does not give work permits to minors ages 14 to 17. Employers need a certificate to hire minors.
duration: 2026 crew members worked June 23 to August 7, 8:30 am to 2:30 pm. Summer hires can keep working Saturdays in the school year.
pay_detail: $18 an hour (2026 crew member rate)

who_can_apply: Ages 15 to 24. Volunteers age 15 to 17 must bring a parent or guardian to orientation. Sites are in Portland Metro, Warm Springs, Central Oregon and Maui, Hawaii.
how_to_apply: Sign up for a monthly orientation on the program page. You can also text YLVol to 85511 or email YLVolunteering@linesforlife.org. Next, you have an interview and training.
notes: The program page asks volunteers to commit to at least one year. Shifts are about 3.5 hours a week.
duration: About 3.5 hours a week for at least one year
pay_detail: Unpaid. The page mentions Work Study positions for young people who face money or other barriers.

who_can_apply: Any student ages 12 to 17 in good standing at school.
how_to_apply: Fill out the application on the Chief Clerk page with your first, second and third choice of dates.
notes: The page asks students to be in good academic standing. The same page lists a 2027 college internship program (not this card).
duration: Honorary page sessions are scheduled on legislative days. The page does not give hours.
pay_detail: Free. Travel and parking are not reimbursed.

who_can_apply: The Salem campus page says youth volunteers must be 16 and finish all training and paperwork. Ages 12 to 15 may volunteer with a parent or guardian over 18. Both apply and train. The Apply Now button says Youth 12 to 17, which conflicts with the 16 minimum. Confirm with the Salem campus.
how_to_apply: Apply at oregonhumane.volunteerportal.org. Use the Youth 12 to 17 button. Do the training and paperwork. Then go to orientation.
notes: The same Oregon Humane page covers both sites. The Salem rules differ from Portland (Portland says 12 to 17, one 2-hour shift every other week for at least 6 months). The Salem text says minimum age 16; the Apply Now button says Youth 12 to 17. min_age is set to 16 to follow the Salem text. Confirm with the Salem campus.
duration: One 2 to 3 hour shift a week after orientation
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Students at least 14 years old from Marion and Polk county school districts. The page lists a questionnaire, references and an essay as application steps.
how_to_apply: Send in the high school student form. Then finish a questionnaire and reference form. The page also mentions an essay and maybe an interview in person.
notes: The general page asks volunteers to commit to a weekly shift for a year. The page does not list a shift time or hours beyond the weekly and summer commitments.
duration: School year: one shift a week, September to June. Summer: two shifts a week for eight weeks, June to August.
pay_detail: Unpaid volunteer role.

who_can_apply: Rising high school juniors and seniors committed to pursuing a four-year college or university. Must be on track to graduate high school in June 2027 or June 2028. The page lists no age requirement.
how_to_apply: Send in the Camp College form on the Willamette page by the deadline.
notes: The page says parents and family are invited to 2 closing sessions. They come before pickup.
duration: 3 days, 2 nights (2026: July 22 to 24)
pay_detail: Free. Meals, housing and transport to college visits are covered. Students get themselves to and from campus.

who_can_apply: A high school break internship. The page does not give grade levels, ages or where you must live. Call or email the farm to ask.
how_to_apply: Watch the High School Opportunities page in February. Call 808-696-5569 with questions. You can also email info@maoorganicfarms.org.
notes: Pay, exact dates and ages are not stated on the page. MA'O also runs college internships, which are not for high schoolers.
duration: 1 week (Fall Break in October, Spring Break in March)
pay_detail: Not stated on the page.
